findings.passage: The escape move does not ease. It shows up in sober stretches as well as using ones: the motel film, released the same week in July 2023 that he told the Standard he was not on drugs, and the interviews of 2025 and 2026.
findings.problem: This is the sentence that 'tips the read to Seven', and the type_hypothesis says the case rests on persistence into sober periods. The dates do not establish that. (1) S09 is dated by its release (2023-07-05). The record has no filming date, so 'released the same week' says nothing about whether he was sober at the motel. The same month he described his sobriety as 'a year total, but split up over like, 5 really bad relapses' (S07). (2) In September 2025 he called himself 'still kind of to this day, like, figuring it out' (S11), so that interview is not a dated sober stretch either. (3) The only 2026 escape instance in the article looks back on his Florida years (see future-02). The 2026 present-tense record mostly shows restraint, which the closing section concedes ('In 2026 the record looks different'). (4) 'Does not ease' is an undated, present-tense absolute about a living person, and the next interview could falsify it while the page still asserts it. As written, the discriminator will not survive the first sober refresh, and it overstates what the record shows now.
findings.acceptance_test: The sentence is dated and limited to what the dated record shows. Example: 'Through 2025 the escape move had not eased, though the record cannot place the motel scene or the 2025 interview in a verified sober stretch.' Either the motel filming date and his sobriety at that time are sourced, or the article no longer counts the motel scene as sober-period evidence. Any 2026 instance cited as current behavior is a present-tense 2026 statement. The 2026 restraint is named as a live complication beside this argument, not only in the closing section. type_hypothesis.discriminator ('Limit: ...') and C91.alternative are updated to match, and confidence stays medium or lower.

I was making music like whenever I was freaked out... I failed a drug test for coke and I remember before we went to jail I had to finish the king of everything song.' The draft's present tense ('works the same way for him') and 'he said in April 2026' turn a 2026 memory of a 2018 habit into evidence of his current practice. That makes it the article's only apparent 2026 escape behavior, which feeds future-01's 'interviews of 2025 and 2026'. The Type 4 rebuttal ('Fike describes songwriting as a way "to not think about shit"') rests on the same quote. In five years, a reader will take this as his practice in 2026.
findings.acceptance_test: The prose makes the timeframe clear, for example: 'Looking back in April 2026 on his Florida years, he said music was where he hid...'. No sentence uses this quote as evidence of 2026 behavior. If a present-tense 2026 instance is wanted, it comes from a 2026 statement about his current practice. One option is S01, summer 2026: 'if you're really songwriting, you don't have the space to feel any of that. It's like running.' Its limit has to be stated: it describes professional pressure falling away in flow, not escape from pain. The claim covering this passage records the retrospective context in its inference or alternative.

findings.acceptance_test: The wording is peak-neutral in both places, e.g. 'reached the top 10 for the first time, at No. 10, on the chart dated October 24, 2026'. assessment: Five-year test: mostly passes on structure, but fails at the pivot. Take away the latest events ('Babydoll' at No. 10 and the October 30, 2026 album) and the portrait still stands. The hook is a July 2023 scene, the spine runs from 2016 to 2025, and the Transformers band-aid is from 2025. The 'why now' paragraph and the ending are dated. Author prose consistently dates quotes that contain time words ('right now', 'still'). 'No public response from Fike had been found as of October 2026' is the right way to handle an unresolved matter. The perishable part is the type argument. The discriminator's sober-period leg rests on a publication date standing in for a filming date (future-01, future-04) and on a 2026 quote about 2018 (future-02). Meanwhile the dated 2026 record leans toward restraint, and the article's own settle signal is likely to get evidence within weeks from release-week press (future-05). I am escalating contested_typing so any refresh runs the full jury. In the metadata, 'three studio albums' will go stale (future-03), the Euphoria season 3 fact is open and untracked (future-06), and the sobriety and chart triggers are not actionable (future-07, future-08). Similarity: the tripped pairs (Florence Pugh, Dylan Patel, Kareem Rahma) share head-triad definitions ('handles fear by...'). I compared those drafts' type sections. The overlap is ordinary type vocabulary and the house's triad-first convention, and the argument around it (motel exit, jail retold three ways, band-aid) is Fike's own, so this is not meaningful reuse. Limits: I opened the cached S10 transcript and S01 text to check timeframes. A web search could not settle season 3 or chart positions after October 24, 2026. I did not re-verify other quotations.
